summary: Requests moving STD 39, BBN Report 1822 describing how a host connects to an IMP, from Standard to Historic status. The interface was the original ARPANET host-to-switch specification and was no longer in use.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo moves the old ARPANET host-to-IMP interface to Historic status. It says the technology is no longer in use and retires STD 39.

subtitle: Moves the obsolete BBN Report 1822 host-to-IMP interface from Standard to Historic.

tldr.problem: BBN Report 1822 described the host-to-IMP interface used by ARPANET, but the RFC says ARPANET technology and the interface were no longer in use.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3109 changes the status of STD 39 from Standard to Historic and retires the STD number.
tldr.outcome: This memo records the retirement of the 1822 interface from active standards status.

today: RFC 3109 moves BBN Report 1822, STD 39, from Standard to Historic status and retires the STD number.

sections.title: The 1822 Host-to-IMP Interface
sections.content:
BBN Report 1822 specified the hardware interface between a host computer and an Interface Message Processor (IMP), the packet switches used in ARPANET. The interface was bit-serial and asynchronous.

Because computers then used different word lengths and the eight-bit byte had not yet become an industry standard, the interface had to accommodate arbitrary word lengths. From a software viewpoint, the report defined ARPANET's link-layer access protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: ARPANET computers connected to packet switches called IMPs. BBN Report 1822 described the hardware interface between them.

sections.title: The Transition Away from 1822
sections.content:
The RFC says the US Department of Defense moved ARPANET technology to TCP/IP in 1983 and split off parts of the network to form MILNET. MILNET IMPs used a mandated byte-oriented, X.25-based interface.

Research ARPANET machines continued using the 1822 interface under the Internet protocol suite, so BBN Report 1822 had been designated STD 39 even though it was not republished as an RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: After the 1983 transition, MILNET used a different interface. Research ARPANET continued with 1822 for a time.

sections.title: Moving STD 39 to Historic
sections.content:
The memo states that ARPANET technology and the BBN 1822 interface are no longer in use. It therefore moves BBN Report 1822 from Standard to Historic status.

The STD number 39 is retired. The RFC says this status change has no known effect on Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC retires STD 39 because the interface is no longer used. It says the change has no known security effect.
